Dê um título curto (3–5 palavras) para:
your last weekend · your job or studies · your city's biggest problem
O professor lê um parágrafo curto e o aluno cria um título:
Many teenagers today sleep less than eight hours a night. Schools start early, homework takes time, and phones keep them awake. As a result, many students feel tired in class.
diga 3 marcadores de opinião do autor.
Palavras de função em títulos (aprenda o que cada uma promete)
effects of / consequences of / impact of
a solution to / ways of dealing with
an example of / a case study

Plastic bags were introduced in the 1960s and quickly became popular because they were cheap and strong. However, it soon became clear that they caused serious environmental damage: they block drains, harm marine animals and take hundreds of years to break down.

In the 19th century, many children worked in factories for up to 14 hours a day. Laws to protect them were introduced slowly, and only after public campaigns revealed the terrible conditions.
Today, schools in Finland start formal reading lessons at the age of seven. Despite this late start, Finnish students consistently perform well in international reading tests.
Some scientists believe that the four-day week could reduce emissions, since fewer people would commute. However, others warn that people may simply travel more on their day off.

content.text: Choose the correct heading for paragraphs A–F from the list below. There are more headings than paragraphs.

i) Why the idea is spreading to other countries · ii) An unexpected benefit for older people · iii) How the scheme began · iv) A common criticism and a response · v) The economic cost of loneliness · vi) Training required for volunteers · vii) Measuring the results · viii) The problem the project aimed to solve · ix) A positive side effect for staff

Across many developed countries, the number of people living alone has risen sharply. Health experts now describe loneliness as a serious public health issue, linked to depression, heart disease and even shorter life expectancy.

In 2015, a small town in the Netherlands decided to act. A local supermarket opened a “chat checkout”, where customers who were in no hurry could stop and talk to the cashier. The idea came from a retired nurse who noticed that some elderly shoppers visited the store every day just to see a friendly face.

Within two years, researchers from a nearby university were asked to evaluate the scheme. They interviewed regular users and found that most felt more connected to their community. Several said the conversations were the only ones they had all day.

Interestingly, the researchers also discovered that the cashiers themselves reported higher job satisfaction. Many said the slower checkout made their work feel more meaningful, which was not one of the original goals.

Not everyone was enthusiastic. Some customers complained that the chat checkouts slowed down service. The company replied that they were optional and that other checkouts remained fast, and complaints soon decreased.
Today, similar initiatives have appeared in Belgium, the UK and Japan, partly because governments are looking for low-cost ways to reduce social isolation in ageing populations.
